title: Why a Windshield Cracks but Holds
coreQuestion: Why does a cracked car windshield stay in one piece?

facts.claim: When it breaks, laminated glass is held in place by an interlayer, typically of polyvinyl butyral, between its layers of glass.
In 1903 the French chemist Édouard Bénédictus dropped a glass flask coated with cellulose nitrate, and it shattered but did not break into pieces.

narration.text: Why does a cracked windshield stay in one piece?
The answer began with a laboratory accident in 1903.
The French chemist Édouard Bénédictus dropped a glass flask coated with a plastic.
It shattered, but it did not break into pieces.
Today the glass layers sandwich a plastic interlayer, typically polyvinyl butyral.
Glass bonded to plastic: it can shatter without falling apart.
